correctness.rationale: Reading ordinary trits low-to-high, the carry after each step is the difference between the read input and its forced output digits divided by the corresponding power of three. Since D is a complete residue system and its digits are nonnegative, inputs below 3^N are representable iff the carry after N trits is zero. The independently reconstructed maps on (-3,-2,-1,0) are (-1,-1,-2,0), (-1,-2,0,0), (-2,0,0,-1). The word 021 resets every state, and the stationary weights scaled by eight are (0,1,2,5). For a fixed most-significant prefix, the unconditioned low-trit block approaches this law; the prefix imposes successive Boolean pullbacks of the terminal zero test. This proves the stated cylinder-mass recursion, with H_e=8F; each depth-m cylinder has mass at most 8*3^(-m), giving continuity. Independent integer enumeration regenerated 14 states and all 42 transitions; the minimum slack of each of the two families of 42 barrier inequalities was 0, and each of the four restricted-root inequalities had zero slack. Induction on ternary endpoints and continuity yield the barriers for all t in [1/3,1]. The root first-level weights are 5,7,3, so F(1/3)=5/24 and F(2/3)=1/2. Dividing by t gives 5/8 and 3/4; a full log-period lies in this interval, with the claimed attaining phases (no uniqueness needed). Zhou's Theorem 1.1 gives the continuous profile and O(1) count error in the complete-residue case. Theorem 1.4 applies since gcd(0,1,5)=1 and gives the same prime-proportion profile up to O(1/log X). Taking sequences X=3^(m+u) proves both sharp prime limits.
residual_risks: The prime result uses the cited prime-transfer theorem; the review checks its statement and hypotheses rather than reproving the analytic number theory. The proof concerns only the stated digit set.
